items.title: Ray Bauduc Interview, 1984-06-27
items.q: I had to have a test, too. That, that's why I was thanking, uh, Harold Peterson's father for the few, few notes that I learned how to read from him, see?

ctx.x: Did the, did you have to have a test to get in the Union, in those days?

Well, yes. I mean, uh, I had to have a test, too. That, that's why I was thanking, uh, Harold Peterson's father for the few, few notes that I learned how to read from him, see? But, uh, I mean, with, well, I don't, I don't know how to say, but in every town, in every place, every politician, every guy that's got a job, he's always a chiseler this way, that way, and, and he allows, allows it to lap over the right way, and the left way. Sometimes you can get in the Union, just, just like Bob Crosby got his chord,…

items.title: Ray Bauduc and Nappy Lamare Interview, 1959-09-09
items.q: Harold Peterson has a music store. Yeah, I know him.

ctx.x: Did you have lessons on your drums when you started?

Well, my dad told me I should take lessons, and I went to Kit Peterson down in New Orleans to take lessons, but I couldn't make the grade. I didn't want to play that kind of music. But the son has the music store? No, he used to teach drums around New Orleans. That's, uh, his father. His father? Harold Peterson has a music store. Yeah, I know him. He's out there on Broad Street, not very far from where I used to live there. I'm on one North White Street.
When did you all ever play together for the first time? Not until the Crosby Band? You must have played down there.
